assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology to incretin-based drugs is a rare complete arc from hormone discovery and mechanism to transformative therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity, with large, clear and lasting clinical impact and growing evidence of broader cardiometabolic benefit.
assessment.attribution: Holst (incretin physiology and GLP-1 secretion/actions), Drucker (GLP-1 biology, receptor and therapeutic concepts) and Mojsov (identification of the biologically active GLP-1 peptide forms) are the decisive scientific contributors among those credited. Knudsen led drug development at a company; industrial credit is a real allocation problem and a three-person limit forces exclusion of other major contributors.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism confirmed independently over decades, drugs widely used with robust outcome trials; recognition is timely and arguably pressing.
uncertainties: Relative priority of Mojsov versus others in peptide identification is debated and I rely on recalled history, not verified here.
Whether the prize should honor basic physiology or the drug development (Knudsen) is unresolved.
Long-term safety of chronic use is still accumulating.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Culture of self-renewing, Lgr5-based adult stem-cell organoids created a general platform for modeling tissue biology, infection, cancer and personalized drug testing, with wide adoption across fields.
assessment.attribution: Clevers identified Lgr5 stem cells and led the organoid derivation; Sato was first author of the key intestinal organoid papers. The credit is fairly concise, though other organoid pioneers (e.g., pluripotent-derived approaches) are outside this candidate's names.
assessment.maturity: Methods reproduced in hundreds of laboratories; clinical translation is still early but the tool-level impact is firmly established.
uncertainties: Clinical impact is largely indirect so far.
Distinction between adult-stem-cell organoids and pluripotent-derived organoids may affect how the prize is framed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered T cells with chimeric antigen receptors produce durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and have opened a new therapeutic modality, with expanding use in autoimmune disease.
assessment.attribution: June (clinical CD19 CAR-T with costimulation, first remissions in CLL), Sadelain (second-generation CD28 design and preclinical foundation) and Rosenberg (adoptive cell transfer and early CAR clinical work) form a defensible trio. Early CAR concepts (Eshhar and others) and the contribution of Rosenberg versus the CAR designers could be contested, since the earliest chimeric receptor work is not in the credited set.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products and years of follow-up; durability evidence strong, though toxicity and access issues persist.
uncertainties: Priority of early chimeric-receptor concepts is not covered by the credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics transformed causal neuroscience by allowing millisecond control of defined cell populations, and has become standard across systems biology, with early therapeutic applications in vision restoration.
assessment.attribution: Nagel and Hegemann established channelrhodopsin as a light-gated cation channel; Deisseroth and Boyden (with Bamberg and Miesenboeck also credited) showed neuronal use. Fair credit with three laureates is difficult because of the number of strong claimants; I favor the channelrhodopsin discoverers plus the principal neuronal-tool developer, acknowledging the disagreement.
assessment.maturity: Technique is thoroughly validated and ubiquitous; recognition is mature, though disease impact is still modest.
uncertainties: Three-person limit leaves Boyden, Bamberg and Miesenboeck out, with real disputes over priority for neuronal use.
Medical impact is limited compared with the research-tool impact.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response defined a fundamental intracellular signaling pathway from the ER to the nucleus, with consequences for secretory physiology, diabetes, neurodegeneration and cancer, and it has led to drug candidates.
assessment.attribution: Mori (Hac1/Ire1 pathway genetics in yeast and mammalian ATF6) and Walter (Ire1 mechanism, unconventional splicing, ISRIB) are the natural pair. Other contributors (e.g., Ron, Harding on PERK) are not in the credited list, so the allocation can be criticized.
assessment.maturity: Mechanistic work is deeply confirmed and conceptually stable; disease-modifying therapeutic validation is still pending.
uncertainties: Clinical translation is not yet proven.
Omission of PERK/ISR work from the credited names may leave attribution incomplete.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Antisense oligonucleotide correction of SMN2 splicing produced nusinersen, the first effective therapy for spinal muscular atrophy, changing a fatal infant disease and validating a general RNA-therapeutic approach.
assessment.attribution: Krainer led the splicing-mechanism work identifying the ISS-N1 target region path and Bennett led antisense chemistry and drug development; this is a clean, small and well-defined credit. Contributions from other groups identifying the target element (e.g., Singh/Singh) may need consideration.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016 with long-term clinical follow-up; strong confirmation, and recognition seems well timed.
uncertainties: Which group first defined the key intronic target is something I am recalling rather than verifying.
Other SMA-directed therapies (gene therapy, small molecules) complicate the story.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rational BCR-ABL inhibition with imatinib turned chronic myeloid leukemia into a manageable disease and established the paradigm of targeted cancer therapy, with enormous impact.
assessment.attribution: Lydon (compound program), Druker (preclinical and clinical proof) and Sawyers (resistance mechanism and next-generation inhibitors) are a natural trio. The upstream discovery of BCR-ABL (Rowley, Witte, Baltimore and others) is outside this candidate and would be a conceptual neighbour.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, with decades of survival data; recognition is arguably overdue, and the field's other prizes (Lasker, Warren) have already honoured these three.
uncertainties: Whether the committee prefers to credit the upstream cancer-genetics discoveries is unclear.
Imatinib was developed in industry, and Novartis chemists are not in the credited set.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identification of BCL11A as the fetal hemoglobin silencer connected human genetic association with a validated therapeutic target and gene-editing therapy for sickle cell disease and beta-thalassemia, a compelling gene-to-therapy story.
assessment.attribution: Thein (human genetic association loci), Sankaran (BCL11A as the repressor) and Orkin (mechanism and enhancer-targeting strategy) cover the discovery arc; Bauer's enhancer-editing work is also strong but I limit to three. The allocation is a real difficulty.
assessment.maturity: Gene-editing therapy approved only recently, so long-term durability is still being assessed; recognition is possibly slightly early.
uncertainties: Durability and access for the editing therapy are not fully established.
Four strong claimants for three slots.
